items.d: 미국 정부의 첨단 반도체 수출 통제가 시행되기 몇 달 전엔 2022년 엔비디아가  중국 스파이 의혹을 받는 인물 앨리스 황에게 중국 알리바바를 직접 소개해줬다고 IT 전문매체 디인포메이션이 익명의 소식통들을 인용해 17일(현지시간) 보도했다.디인포메이션에 따르면 엔비디아 영업팀이 다리를 놓아준 2022년은 인공지능(AI) 열풍이 본격화하기 전으로, 당시 엔비디아의 연간 총매출은 270억 달러(현재의 약 10분의 1 수준)에 불과했다. 아시아 최대 클라우드 기업이었던 알리바바는 엔비디아의 최첨단 칩 ‘A100’의 핵심 구매자였다.당시 클라우드 기업 대상 칩 대여 사업을 막 구상하던 앨리스 황은 엔비디아의 소개로 알리바바라는 대형 고객사를 확보했다. 이를 발판 삼아 은행 대출까지 받아 엔비디아 칩 구매 자금을

items.t: 엔비디아 훈풍에 5000피 회복…로봇·엔터주 '훨훨'
items.fullText: 투자 인사이트 오늘의 투자포인트 엔비디아 훈풍에 5000피 회복…로봇·엔터주 '훨훨' 입력 2026.11.18 15:54 수정 2026.11.18 15:55 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 고정삼 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 코스피·코스닥 2% 가까이 상승 삼전 2%·하이닉스 4% 넘게 올라 사진=연합뉴스 코스피지수가 18일 기관투자가의 매수세에 2% 가까이 상승해 하루 만에 5000선을 회복했다. 엔비디아 의 3분기 호실적에 인공지능(AI) 수요 둔화 우려가 일부 완화되면서 반도체주 중심으로 매수세가 유입됐다. 이날 코스피지수는 전장보다 98.96포인트(1.99%) 오른 5067.44로 마감해 심리적 지지선으로 일컬어지는 5000선을 회복했다. 2.62% 상승 출발한 코스피지수는 오전장 초반 3% 넘게 오름폭을 확대한 뒤 하락 전환하는 등 높은 변동성을 보였다. 이후 오전 11시57분께를 기점으로 상승 전환해 추세를 굳혔다. 유가증권시장에서 기관이 5492억원어치를 사들이며 지수 상승을 이끌었고 개인과 외국인은 각각 6699억원과 3276억원어치를 팔았다. 장 초반 '사자'에 나섰던 외국인은 '팔자'로 돌아서면서 4거래일 연속 순매도세를 이어갔다. 엔비디아가 이날 시장의 예상을 넘어서는 3분기 실적을 발표하면서 시장 전반의 투자심리가 개선된 것으로 분석된다. 엔비디아는 2027회계연도 3분기(8∼10월) 매출액이 지난해 같은 기간보다 103% 늘어난 1158억달러(약 155조원)를 기록해 시장 전망치(1091억달러)를 웃돌았다. 데이터센터 매출액도 110% 증가한 1176억달러로 예상치인 1018억달러를 넘어섰다. 4분기 매출 전망치 역시 시장의 전망보다 높은 1300억달러를 제시했다. 이 영향으로 반도체 대장주 삼성전자 (2.31%)와 SK 하이닉스 (4.19%)가 강세로 마감했다. 엔비디아 밸류체인(가치사슬)에 속한 두산 (8.69%)도 급등했다. 이밖에 코스피 시가총액 상위 종목 중 삼성전기 (7.43%) SK스퀘어 (4.42%) 삼성생명 (5.37%) 현대차 (3.09%) 등이 올랐고 삼성바이오로직스 (-3.39%) 셀트리온 (-2.58%) KB금융 (-0.26%) LG 에너지솔루션(-0.16%) 등이 내렸다. 코스닥지수는 전장보다 12.75포인트(1.96%) 오른 662.81로 마감했다. 2.29% 상승 출발한 코스닥지수 역시 장 초반 3% 넘게 오름폭을 키운 뒤 일부 반납하는 흐름을 보였다. 코스닥시장에서도 기관이 1893억원어치를 사들였고 개인과 외국인이 각각 1440억원과 334억원어치를 팔았다. 이날 피지컬 AI 기대감이 부각되면서 레인보우로보틱스 (20.06%) 로보티즈 (13.24%) 로보스타 (9.34%) 현대오토에버 (8.99%) 등 로봇주가 동반 급등했다. 또 한중 문화 콘텐츠 교류 논의 소식에 에스엠 (14.3%) JYP 엔터(8.72%) 와이지엔터테인먼트 (4.92%) 등 엔터주가 수혜 기대감에 힘입어 일제히 강세로 마감했다. 고정삼 한경닷컴 기자 jsk@hankyung.com 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. AI 포인트 뷰 이전 분석 종목 다음 분석 종목 본 서비스의 AI가 제공하는 종목 정보는 정보 제공 목적의 참고 자료일 뿐, 투자 권유·자문·추천에 해당하지 않습니다. 투자에 따른 손실 책임

items.t: "삼전닉스에 또 돈벼락 쏟아지나"…엔비디아가 꺼낸 '비장의 카드'
items.fullText: 산업 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 "삼전닉스에 또 돈벼락 쏟아지나"…엔비디아가 꺼낸 '비장의 카드' 입력 2026.11.18 15:32 수정 2026.11.18 15:45 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 홍민성 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 엔비디아 또 사상 최대실적…삼전닉스 '메모리 수혜' 더 커진다 엔비디아, 3분기 매출 1158억달러 기록 '효자' 데이터센터…전년 대비 110%↑ 베라 루빈 출하 개시…HBM4 수요 확대 기대 사진=한경DB 엔비디아가 올해 3분기 매출을 전년보다 두 배 이상 늘리며 사상 최대 실적을 기록했다. 차세대 AI 플랫폼 '베라 루빈'의 출하까지 본격화하면서 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스에도 성장 기회가 열리고 있다는 분석이 나온다. 특히 고대역폭메모리(HBM) 신제품인 HBM4와 서버용 D램 수요가 확대될 것으로 예상된다. 엔비디아 매출 1158억달러…데이터센터가 93% 18일 업계에 따르면 엔비디아는 전날(현지시간) 발표한 2027회계연도 3분기(8~10월) 실적에서 매출 1158억4400만달러를 기록했다. 전년 동기 대비 103%, 직전 분기보다 20% 증가한 규모다. 시장 예상치인 약 1091억달러도 웃돌았다. 영업이익은 775억달러로 지난해 같은 기간보다 115% 늘었다. 매출 증가를 이끈 것은 데이터센터 사업이다. 3분기 데이터센터 매출은 1076억달러로 전년 동기보다 110% 급증했다. 전체 매출의 약 93%에 달한다. 글로벌 빅테크 기업들의 AI 인프라 투자가 이어지면서 관련 반도체와 시스템 판매가 크게 늘어난 것으로 풀이된다. 엔비디아는 2027회계연도 4분기 매출 전망치로 1300억달러를 제시했다. 오차 범위는 ±3%다. 시장 예상치인 약 1250억달러를 웃도는 수준이다. 이번 전망에는 중국 데이터센터용 컴퓨팅 사업 매출을 반영하지 않았다. 다만 4분기에는 통상적인 회계 분기보다 1주가 더 포함된다. 차세대 AI 플랫폼 '베라 루빈 NVL72'의 출하가 시작된 점도 눈에 띈다. 엔비디아는 이번 실적 발표에서 베라 루빈 생산량을 늘리고 고객사에 제품 공급을 시작했다고 밝혔다. 구글 클라우드와 마이크로소프트 애저, 오라클 클라우드, 코어위브 등 주요 클라우드 사업자들이 관련 시스템을 도입하고 있다. 엔비디아 로고 / 로이터 연합뉴스 GPU 72개에 HBM4 20.7TB…삼전닉스 공급 확대 기회 베라 루빈은 기존 블랙웰을 잇는 엔비디아의 차세대 AI 플랫폼이다. 핵심 시스템인 NVL72는 루빈 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 72개와 베라 중앙처리장치(CPU) 36개를 하나의 랙에 통합했다. GPU 1개에 288기가바이트(GB)의 HBM4가 탑재되며 전체 HBM4 용량은 약 20.7테라바이트(TB)에 달한다. 글로벌 시장조사업체 카운터포인트리서치는 엔비디아의 차세대 플랫폼 전환이 국내 메모리 반도체 기업에 긍정적으로 작용할 것으로 분석했다. AI 모델이 대형화하고 연산량이 늘어나면서 데이터를 빠르게 처리하는 고성능 메모리의 중요성이 커지고 있기 때문이다. 베라 루빈에 적용되는 HBM4는 기존 세대보다 높은 대역폭과 용량을 제공하는 제품이다. 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스도 HBM4 공급 확대에 속도를 내고 있다. SK하이닉스는 지난달 3분기 실적 발표에서 올해 4분기 HBM4 출하량과 매출이 모두 HBM3E를 넘어설 것으로 예상했다. 연말까지 청주 M15X 공장의 생산능력을 최대 수준으로 끌어올려 HBM4 생산을 확대할 계획이다. 삼성전자 역시 3분기 HBM4 판매량을 크게 늘렸다고 밝혔다. 올해 4분기에는 HBM과 서버용 D램, 솔리드스테이트드라이브(SSD) 등 AI 관련 제품 판매를 확대한다는 방침이다. 차세대 CPU·GPU 플랫폼에 맞춘 메모리 제품을 중심으로 수요가

items.t: Nvidia enters the post-Jensen Huang era with a bang
items.d: Nvidia delivered a message with its first earnings report under new leadership: The sky isn’t falling.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Nvidia enters the post-Jensen Huang era with a bang The company’s interim CEO delivered strong earnings and a clear message about the future of Nvidia without its charismatic former leader. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 NVIDIA says Jensen Huang will not return as CEO 01:47 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 17, 2026, 9:41 PM EST / Updated Nov. 17, 2026, 9:42 PM EST By David Ingram Nvidia delivered a message with its first earnings report under new leadership: The sky isn’t falling. With a new CEO and board chair just days after the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang, the company reported results Tuesday that beat analysts’ expectations for AI chip sales. Nvidia’s new leaders also appeared to calm some investors’ nerves about the immediate future of a company at the heart of the AI economy. Colette Kress, the interim CEO and Nvidia’s longtime chief financial officer, and Harvey Jones, the newly elected board chair, used the quarterly earnings call to answer many — but not all — of the biggest questions hanging over Nvidia, including who will be running things in the near term. Just hours before the earnings release, Huang had injected fresh uncertainty into precisely that question when announced that he would be “honored” to return to the job of CEO, if the company’s board decided to bring him back. NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean.
